what_its_for: Sotorasib is a cancer medicine used to treat adults with a certain type of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has spread to other parts of the body. It works specifically for patients whose cancer has a particular gene change called KRAS G12C mutation. Your doctor will test your tumor to confirm this mutation before starting treatment.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablets whole with or without food. Do not crush, break, or chew the tablets. Try to take your dose at the same time each day to help you remember. If you vomit after taking your dose, do NOT take another dose that day — just take your next scheduled dose as planned.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 960 mg (eight 120 mg tablets) taken by mouth once daily. Your doctor may lower your dose or temporarily stop your treatment if you experience certain side effects. Always take the exact dose your doctor prescribes and never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your regular dose on schedule. Never take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store sotorasib tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep them in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect them from moisture and heat. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use tablets past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium (such as Maalox, Mylanta, or Tums) within 4 hours before or 10 hours after taking sotorasib, as they can reduce how well the medicine works. Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take, as many drugs can interact with sotorasib — especially stomach acid reducers (proton pump inhibitors like omeprazole). Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice. Women should avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: new or worsening shortness of breath or cough (could be a lung problem called pneumonitis); yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain (signs of liver problems); diarrhea that is severe or does not go away; muscle or joint pain that is severe; fever, chills, or signs of infection; or any unusual bleeding. Also call your doctor before starting any new medication, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements.
when_it_works: Sotorasib does not work overnight. It may take several weeks before your doctor can tell if the medicine is working, usually through follow-up scans or tests. It is very important to keep taking your medicine every day even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Women who are pregnant or breastfeeding should NOT use sotorasib, as it can harm an unborn baby or a nursing infant. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 3 months after the last dose. Male patients with female partners who can become pregnant should use contraception during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose. If you have liver problems, tell your doctor, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Safety and effectiveness in children has not been established.
